component.name: ArchiveFree
component.summary: Look inside archives before unpacking them

description.p: ArchiveFree opens zip, 7z, rar and tar files in a window so you can see what is inside before anything is written to disk. Browse the folders, check the file sizes, preview a document, and then extract everything — or just the two files you actually wanted.

ul.li: Opens zip, 7z, rar, tar (gz, bz2, xz, zst), iso, cab, deb, rpm and more
Browse the contents as folders, with sizes, types and dates
Extract everything, or only what you select, anywhere you choose
Preview text, code and images without extracting the archive
Asks before overwriting — it never silently replaces your files
Create archives with a password or split into parts
Large archives never freeze the window, and every operation can be cancelled

description.p: No adverts, no telemetry, no accounts and no paid tiers. Free software, for good.

screenshot.caption: Browse an archive's contents before extracting anything
Choose exactly where files go, with no surprises
Preview a file without extracting the archive
Create an archive in a few clicks

ul.li: Install advice for missing helper programs now matches the distribution — dnf on Fedora, pacman on Arch, zypper on openSUSE — with the correct package name for each. It previously told everyone to run an apt command
The first run offers to add right-click menu entries, naming the file manager it found. Thunar and Nautilus store this per user, so a system package cannot set it up for you

description.p: Fixes the right-click menu on XFCE.

ul.li: Thunar's custom-action file uses a non-standard XML declaration that Python refused to parse, so the right-click entries silently failed to install on XFCE — the desktop where they matter most
Menu entries now name ArchiveFree, so they are distinguishable from the archive plugin's own "Extract Here"
The settings page can see the host's file managers from inside the Flatpak

description.p: Bug fixes found by an expanded test suite.

ul.li: Archives named .tgz, .txz, .tbz2 and .tzst are now recognised as tar archives instead of opening as a single unnamed blob
An empty file is no longer identified as an archive by its name alone
Extraction now defaults to the folder the archive is in, rather than wherever you last extracted something
Browse and extract zip, 7z, rar, tar and single-stream archives
Create zip, 7z and tar archives, optionally with a password or split into parts
One-click, reversible option to become the default archive application
